input_facts.text:
On 1 May 2024 the FOMC left its target range at 5.25–5.50 percent and announced continued securities runoff.
The Treasury monthly redemption cap remains $60 billion for May and becomes $25 billion on 1 June. The agency debt/MBS cap stays $35 billion.
Interest on reserve balances remains 5.4 percent, effective 2 May.

adjudication_excerpt.text: Announcing a future implementation date does not make that policy effective on announcement day. The Treasury runoff ceiling falls $35 billion per month, or 58.33 percent, from June; this is a cap change, not realized runoff or an asset-purchase amount. May still has the $60 billion cap. Slower runoff does not establish QE, a policy-rate cut, a $35 billion reserve injection or a market return.

question_en: After the May 1 announcement, which Treasury cap applies during May and from June 1? Quantify the change and distinguish announcement, implementation, actual runoff, reserves and the policy rate. Use only these supplied facts.

expected_properties.check: May cap is $60B/month; $25B/month begins June 1. The May 2 interest-on-reserves date is separate.
Treasury cap reduction is $35B/month, or 58.33% of $60B; agency cap stays $35B.
A lower runoff ceiling is not an actual $35B asset purchase, measured reserve addition or completed runoff observation.
Policy range remains 5.25–5.50%; no supplied market response or historically captured snapshot is established.

known_failure_modes: Apply the June Treasury cap in May because it was announced on May 1.
Confuse the $35B change with the distinct $35B agency cap or realized purchases.
Treat a retrieved publication label or Last-Modified header as immutable historical byte proof.
gold_standard_sentence: May retains the $60B Treasury cap; June starts $25B, a $35B/month (58.33%) cap reduction. The agency cap and policy-rate range are unchanged. This is slower intended runoff, with no demonstrated purchase, reserve injection or return.
